      From house calls to video consults: NSW opens new doors for vets

      NSW reforms could unlock new revenue streams for vets in a pet healthcare market worth $6.1 billion, according to Animal Medicines Australia.
      Simon Thompson
      Nov 24, 2026 3 min read

      Share

      0
      Prefer SmartCompany
      Listen to audio version of this article
      Sponsored by
      0:00 / 3:38
      Instaread

      New laws in New South Wales could pave the way for more mobile veterinary businesses and unlock new income streams for established operators.

      The Veterinary Services Bill 2026, passed by the NSW parliament last week, establishes a new licensing framework for veterinary businesses, including mobile practices, and paves the way for remote prescribing in urgent cases.

      New opportunities for mobile veterinary businesses

      The reforms create a clearer licensing pathway for mobile veterinary practices, which could see an increase in the number of vets setting up their own practice.

      Dr Claire Jenkins, veterinarian and founder of telehealth platform VetChat, told SmartCompany the changes will give vets more tools to offer pet owners.

      “They will be able to charge for remote consultations and they will be able to provide them access to medication,” she said.

      “This is a win for mobile veterinarians as well, particularly how they’ll be able to engage with pet owners.”

      Related Article Block Placeholder Article ID: 322212

      Heidi Health goes fur-ther with AI for pet care
      Tegan Jones

      Kwan Yun, of Sydney-based North Shore Mobile Vet, told SmartCompany mobile practices could command a premium for the convenience they offer pet owners.

      “It is set to be more expensive than a local vet because I’m cutting their [travel] time out for them,” Yun said.

      Growing demand due to veterinary workforce shortages

      Australians spent $6.1 billion on veterinary care and related pet health products and services in 2024–25, according to Animal Medicines Australia.

      However, Dr Lisa Chimes, an emergency veterinarian and founder of DOG & CAT by Dr Lisa, said growth in the veterinary workforce had failed to keep pace with the surge in pet ownership during COVID-19.

      “There is a rising demand for pet care due to increased pet ownership during COVID and there is also a greater willingness of pet parents to care for their pets at a higher standard, but this doesn’t line up with the nationwide shortage of vets and vet nurses,” she said.

      VetChat is already hiring more vets to keep up with this demand.

      “We are doing over 100,000 consultations a year right now,” Jenkins said.

      “We are growing each month. So absolutely we are employing more veterinarians to meet the growing demand.”

      VetChat currently operates as a triage service, where animal owners seek advice about whether their pet needs to see a vet and how urgently.

      The reforms will enable telehealth providers to go one step further and give pet owners access to certain medications, including pain relief, in urgent cases where in-person care is unavailable.

      Jenkins said financial stress, rural isolation, lack of mobility and veterinary workforce shortages are increasingly preventing pet owners from accessing veterinary care.

      “Vets are stretched especially in the regions and many clinics just simply can’t staff a 24/7 operation,” she said.

      “After hours care is often the hardest bit to keep going.”

      Related Article Block Placeholder Article ID: 348670

      AI-powered telehealth startup Doccy wins 2026 Smart50 Rising Star award
      David Adams AND Adam Bub

      Further changes could follow

      Under the NSW changes, veterinarians will be permitted to prescribe certain medications following a live video consultation in urgent cases where delaying treatment risks animal suffering or deterioration.

      Prescriptions will be limited to medication reasonably required until the animal can receive in-person care.

      The legislation provides for a review after three years, to assess the impact of the reforms on veterinary businesses, telehealth uptake, and access to care in regional NSW.

      Jenkins said the changes presented an opportunity to demonstrate the safety of remote prescribing before potentially expanding the rules.

      “This is a real opportunity to help people that aren’t getting access to help now and demonstrate its safety and then progress rules based on data,” she said.

      The bill is awaiting royal assent, with the costs and details of the new licensing framework yet to be finalised.

      Manage your data

      You can choose how your personal data is used. Vendors want your permission to do the following:

      Purposes

      View details

      Create profiles for personalised advertising

Your profile can be used (also later) to present advertising that appears more relevant based on your possible interests by this and other entities.

      Use profiles to select personalised advertising

      Advertising presented to you on this service can be based on your advertising profiles, which can reflect your activity on this service or other websites or apps (like the forms you submit, content you look at), possible interests and personal aspects.

      Create profiles to personalise content

      Content presented to you on this service can be based on your content personalisation profiles, which can reflect your activity on this or other services (for instance, the forms you submit, content you look at), possible interests and personal aspects.       Measure advertising performance

      Information regarding which advertising is presented to you and how you interact with it can be used to determine how well an advert has worked for you or other users and whether the goals of the advertising were reached. For instance, whether you saw an ad, whether you clicked on it, whether it led you to buy a product or visit a website, etc. This is very helpful to understand the relevance of advertising campaigns.

      View details

      Measure content performance

      Information regarding which content is presented to you and how you interact with it can be used to determine whether the (non-advertising) content e.g. reached its intended audience and matched your interests. For instance, whether you read an article, watch a video, listen to a podcast or look at a product description, how long you spent on this service and the web pages you visit etc. This is very helpful to understand the relevance of (non-advertising) content that is shown to you.

      View details

      Understand audiences through statistics or combinations of data from different sources

      Reports can be generated based on the combination of data sets (like user profiles, statistics, market research, analytics data) regarding your interactions and those of other users with advertising or (non-advertising) content to identify common characteristics (for instance, to determine which target audiences are more receptive to an ad campaign or to certain contents).

      View details

      Develop and improve services

      Information about your activity on this service, such as your interaction with ads or content, can be very helpful to improve products and services and to build new products and services based on user interactions, the type of audience, etc. This specific purpose does not include the development or improvement of user profiles and identifiers.

      View details

      Use limited data to select content

      Content presented to you on this service can be based on limited data, such as the website or app you are using, your non-precise location, your device type, or which content you are (or have been) interacting with (for example, to limit the number of times a video or an article is presented to you).

      Special purposes

      Ensure security, prevent and detect fraud, and fix errors

      Save and communicate privacy choices

      Features

      These means of processing can be used solely in pursuit of one or several purposes for which you are given a choice in this notice.

      Match and combine data from other data sources

      Information about your activity on this service may be matched and combined with other information relating to you and originating from various sources (for instance your activity on a separate online service, your use of a loyalty card in-store, or your answers to a survey), in support of the purposes explained in this notice.

      View details

      Link different devices

      In support of the purposes explained in this notice, your device might be considered as likely linked to other devices that belong to you or your household (for instance because you are logged in to the same service on both your phone and your computer, or because you may use the same Internet connection on both devices).

      Identify devices based on information transmitted automatically

      Your device might be distinguished from other devices based on information it automatically sends when accessing the Internet (for instance, the IP address of your Internet connection or the type of browser you are using) in support of the purposes exposed in this notice.

      How this consent management platform (CMP) works:

      CMP privacy choices

      Storage, duration, and usage details

      The choices you make with this CMP regarding the purposes and entities will affect how personalized advertising is presented to you. We need to store these choices to respect them on future visits, and they are stored differently based on the type of site or app you're using:
      • For sites, your choices are saved in a cookie named “FCCDCF” for a maximum duration of 390 days.
      • For apps, your choices are saved in device storage prefixed by “IABTCF_”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this app.
      • For accelerated mobile page (AMP) sites, your choices are saved in local storage prefixed by “amp-store”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this site.
